findings.body: The request is rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the role is treated as a team administrator elsewhere and the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.
findings.failure_mode: Valid team administrators cannot use the add-guests endpoint.
findings.impact: The request is rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the role is treated as a team administrator elsewhere and the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.
findings.root_cause: The authorization expression combines the admin and owner predicates with &&.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an OR authorization check (or isTeamAdmin alone, since it already includes OWNER) instead of requiring both admin and owner membership checks.
findings.title: Allow team admins to add guests
findings.trigger: An accepted member whose role is ADMIN, but not OWNER, adds guests to a booking for that team.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 47-48 show `isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Repository context confirms isTeamAdmin already matches ADMIN or OWNER roles (L270: OR [{role:ADMIN},{role:OWNER}]). Using && requires both checks to pass, so an ADMIN who is not OWNER gets false. Variable name suggests OR was intended.

findings.body: Each duplicate passes the later existing-attendee filter and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows, leading to duplicate calendar recipients and email notifications.
findings.failure_mode: One add-guests request can create multiple attendee records for the same guest.
findings.impact: Each duplicate passes the later existing-attendee filter and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows, leading to duplicate calendar recipients and email notifications.
findings.root_cause: The server-side input schema validates each email but imposes no array uniqueness constraint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a schema refinement that rejects duplicate normalized email addresses before the handler performs createMany.
findings.title: Reject duplicate guest addresses at the API boundary
findings.trigger: A direct tRPC caller submits the same valid email address more than once in a single guests array.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 5 shows schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refinement. Handler filters against existing attendees but not duplicates within the input array itself. createMany would insert duplicate rows for repeated emails in a single request.

findings.body: The blocked address is accepted, added as an attendee, and sent booking information despite the blacklist.
findings.failure_mode: Case variants bypass the configured guest-email blocklist.
findings.impact: The blocked address is accepted, added as an attendee, and sent booking information despite the blacklist.
findings.root_cause: Blacklist entries are lowercased while submitted guest values are compared without normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize each submitted guest address, and preferably blacklist configuration entries, to the same case before comparison.
findings.title: Normalize guest emails before applying the blacklist
findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains a blocked lowercase address and a caller submits the same address using uppercase or mixed-case characters.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 70-77 show blacklist is lowercased but guest comparison uses `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing guest. A mixed-case variant of a blocked address bypasses the check.

pr.title: feat: ability to add guests via app.cal.com/bookings

raw_findings.body: The request is rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the role is treated as a team administrator elsewhere and the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid team administrators cannot use the add-guests endpoint.
raw_findings.impact: The request is rejected with FORBIDDEN even though the role is treated as a team administrator elsewhere and the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.
raw_findings.root_cause: The authorization expression combines the admin and owner predicates with &&.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use an OR authorization check (or isTeamAdmin alone, since it already includes OWNER) instead of requiring both admin and owner membership checks.
raw_findings.title: Allow team admins to add guests
raw_findings.trigger: An accepted member whose role is ADMIN, but not OWNER, adds guests to a booking for that team.

raw_findings.body: Each duplicate passes the later existing-attendee filter and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows, leading to duplicate calendar recipients and email notifications.
raw_findings.failure_mode: One add-guests request can create multiple attendee records for the same guest.
raw_findings.impact: Each duplicate passes the later existing-attendee filter and createMany inserts duplicate Attendee rows, leading to duplicate calendar recipients and email notifications.
raw_findings.root_cause: The server-side input schema validates each email but imposes no array uniqueness constraint.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a schema refinement that rejects duplicate normalized email addresses before the handler performs createMany.
raw_findings.title: Reject duplicate guest addresses at the API boundary
raw_findings.trigger: A direct tRPC caller submits the same valid email address more than once in a single guests array.

raw_findings.body: The blocked address is accepted, added as an attendee, and sent booking information despite the blacklist.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Case variants bypass the configured guest-email blocklist.
raw_findings.impact: The blocked address is accepted, added as an attendee, and sent booking information despite the blacklist.
raw_findings.root_cause: Blacklist entries are lowercased while submitted guest values are compared without normalization.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize each submitted guest address, and preferably blacklist configuration entries, to the same case before comparison.
raw_findings.title: Normalize guest emails before applying the blacklist
raw_findings.trigger: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS contains a blocked lowercase address and a caller submits the same address using uppercase or mixed-case characters.

raw_findings.body: The existing attendee is classified as a newly added guest and receives a normal booking-confirmation email rather than the guests-added notification, although no attendee record was added for them.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Notification type does not reflect which attendees were actually added.
raw_findings.impact: The existing attendee is classified as a newly added guest and receives a normal booking-confirmation email rather than the guests-added notification, although no attendee record was added for them.
raw_findings.root_cause: Email recipient classification uses the unfiltered request array instead of the filtered list that was persisted.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass uniqueGuests to sendAddGuestsEmails so its new-guest classification matches the rows created by the handler.
raw_findings.title: Use the actually added guests when selecting notification templates
raw_findings.trigger: A request contains both an address already present on the booking and at least one new address.

raw_findings.body: Host and attendee emails are still sent for the guest addition, contrary to the event type's standard-email suppression setting.
raw_findings.impact: Host and attendee emails are still sent for the guest addition, contrary to the event type's standard-email suppression setting.
raw_findings.root_cause: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally queues host and attendee mail and receives no event metadata to evaluate suppression settings.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Accept the event-type metadata in sendAddGuestsEmails, pass it from the handler, and guard host and attendee queues with eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail as the other booking-notification functions do.
raw_findings.title: Honor event-type standard-email suppression for guest additions
raw_findings.trigger: Guests are added to an event type configured with disableStandardEmails.all.host and/or disableStandardEmails.all.attendee.

raw_findings.body: Only the organizer receives the guest-added host notification; the team-member notification branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs because the constructed CalendarEvent has no team or members.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Team members are omitted from guest-addition notifications.
raw_findings.impact: Only the organizer receives the guest-added host notification; the team-member notification branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs because the constructed CalendarEvent has no team or members.
raw_findings.root_cause: The booking query only loads scalar event-type data and the CalendarEvent construction never supplies a team property.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Load the event type's team and members, map them into evt.team, and preserve that team data when calling sendAddGuestsEmails.
raw_findings.title: Populate team data before sending add-guests notifications
raw_findings.trigger: Guests are added to a team event with team members other than the booking organizer.

raw_findings.body: The EventManager is initialized with the caller's credentials rather than the credential that owns the booking's calendar event, so the organizer's external calendar can remain without the newly added guest.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Database attendees and external calendar attendees can diverge for delegated guest additions.
raw_findings.impact: The EventManager is initialized with the caller's credentials rather than the credential that owns the booking's calendar event, so the organizer's external calendar can remain without the newly added guest.
raw_findings.root_cause: The handler authorizes non-organizers but always fetches credentials from ctx.user.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize EventManager with the booking organizer and the credentials associated with the booking/calendar references, rather than the non-organizer caller's credentials.
raw_findings.title: Update calendars with the booking organizer's credentials
raw_findings.trigger: An authorized attendee or a team owner modifies a booking organized by another user whose calendar reference uses that organizer's private calendar credential.

finding.verifier_reason: Patch line 158 shows `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` regardless of who the organizer is. Authorization allows attendees/team admins to call this. EventManager initialized with caller's credentials cannot update organizer's external calendar when credentials differ.
